_comment: Three cart journeys. Unlike the other data files these are NOT rows of one
shape: each has its own basket and its own ending, so each is a named object
loaded with loadCase() rather than a row loaded with loadCases().
Each journey is a single test rather than a row run many times, so its title
and tags are written at the test() call in the spec, not here. This file holds
only the values the journey acts on.
'removeThenBuyLaptop.remove' holds titles taken from its own 'add' list. What
survives is derived by the spec, so the data cannot claim to keep something it
'emptiedThenOrder' asks for three monitors and DemoBlaze sells only two, so
'ASUS Full HD' is listed twice. That duplicate is deliberate: it is what makes
the basket six items, and it is why the cart is emptied by row index rather
Titles are chosen so none is a substring of another — cart rows are matched by
text, so 'Sony vaio i5' beside 'Sony vaio i7' would be ambiguous.
Expiry dates are tokens expanded at run time by utils/dates.ts, so
'{{year+2}}' is always a card that has not expired.

outcome.shouldHaveBeen: Place Order should be unavailable, or the order refused, when the cart holds no items. Emptying a filled cart reaches the same defect as never filling one: the basket is verified to hold six items and then verified to hold none, and the order is still taken.
